question: Why do offenses run when passing gains more?

notes.models_not_ours: epa, wp, wpa and xpass are nflfastR's models, used as given
notes.intervals: 95% percentile intervals from 1000 resamples of whole games
notes.scrambles: counted as pass (nflverse records them as runs)

team_tendency.unit: change in the outcome per 10 percentage points of pass rate in other games

pass_epa_slope_needed_for_todays_mix_to_.unit: EPA per pass per 10 percentage points of pass rate

within_game.unit: EPA per play per 10 percentage points of pass share over the window

run_yards_histogram.note: ends are clipped: -10 means 10 or more lost, 40 means 40 or more gained

pass_yards_histogram.note: ends are clipped: -10 means 10 or more lost, 40 means 40 or more gained

protecting_a_late_lead.note: seconds_elapsed is game clock from this snap to the next snap, including plays after which the defense called timeout, the two-minute warning fell, the ball went out of bounds or a team scored. clock_cost_to_defense adds timeout_seconds for each timeout the defense spent, a rough index and not a model. docs/research/endgame_clock.md has the cleaner split (in-bounds run by a leader 43 seconds, incompletion 5).

protecting_a_lead_whole_fourth_quarter.note: seconds_elapsed is game clock from this snap to the next snap, including plays after which the defense called timeout, the two-minute warning fell, the ball went out of bounds or a team scored. clock_cost_to_defense adds timeout_seconds for each timeout the defense spent, a rough index and not a model. docs/research/endgame_clock.md has the cleaner split (in-bounds run by a leader 43 seconds, incompletion 5).

run_sets_up_the_pass.note_previous_play: previous called play of the same drive; down, distance bin, field bin and season held fixed; neutral early downs

check_against_endgame_clock_note.definition: downs 1 to 3, fourth quarter, last 2:00, leading by 1 to 8

how_much_survives.unit: nflfastR EPA per play, pass minus run

points_left_on_the_table_upper_bound.caveats: nflfastR EPA units. Assumes the shifted runs would gain what the average pass gains in the same down, distance and field cell and that defenses do not respond; any response lowers it, so read it as an upper bound. The interval covers sampling noise only. Covers neutral early downs only.

fit.what: q2 run and pass outcome tables

hook.note: counts of what happened when teams chose each play type; not what would happen if a team changed its mix
